headline: GOLD IS NO. 2: ECB Report Shows Bullion Overtakes US Treasuries at 27% of Global Reserves
snippet: The European Central Bank's annual Financial Integration report, released this week, reveals that gold has displaced US Treasuries as the world's second-largest reserve asset — accounting for 27% of total central bank reserves at end-2025, up from 20% a year earlier, while US Treasuries fell to 22% from 25%. Central bank net purchases totalled 850 tonnes in 2025, with China, Poland, Turkey, and India among the largest buyers; ECB President Lagarde attributed the structural shift to geopolitical tensions and a deliberate diversification away from dollar-denominated assets following Washington's 2022 freezing of Russian reserves. For junior mining investors, the fact that global central banks are now formally allocating more to physical gold than to the world's benchmark safe-haven bond means the institutional bid underpinning gold's premium pricing environment is structural — not speculative — and provides the demand floor that makes current levels, even after the June correction from $5,589, historically well-supported.

headline: ECB HIKES TO 2.25% AND PPI HITS 6.5% — Gold and Silver ROSE Anyway on June 12
snippet: Gold and silver advanced on June 12 despite a textbook double bearish combination: the European Central Bank raised its deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.25% — its first hike since September 2023 — while US May PPI data came in at 6.5% year-over-year, reinforcing Fed rate-hike expectations ahead of Kevin Warsh's first FOMC press conference on June 16-17. That both metals held and rose against simultaneous hawkish central bank action from Europe and hot US producer price inflation is structurally significant: historically, precious metals that resist rate-hike catalysts are discounting a market perception that current inflation is supply-driven and persistent — precisely the case with Iran-conflict energy prices driving the bulk of the May PPI. For investors calibrating entry points before next week's FOMC, June 12's performance provides the clearest evidence yet that the structural bid is overriding near-term bearish catalysts.

headline: GOLD MINERS BPI CRASHES TO ZERO: Total Capitulation Mirrors September 2022 Bottom Before 170%+ Rally
snippet: The Gold Miners Bullish Percent Index (BPGDM) hit 0.00 on June 9, 2026 — meaning literally zero gold mining stocks are in a technical uptrend by point-and-figure methodology, a condition Richard Mills identifies as total capitulation. The only comparable extreme in recent history was late September 2022, which was the exact cycle bottom; the recovery that followed saw gold appreciate over 170% across the subsequent multi-year bull phase. Mills frames the signal as a contrarian opportunity: maximum pessimism is not a warning, it is the precondition for the face-ripping short-covering rally that oversold extremes historically precede. With gold holding the $4,150-4,200 range against stacked bearish catalysts and institutional year-end targets clustering between $5,200 and $6,000, a BPGDM reading of zero represents the widest gap between technical despair and fundamental conviction in the current cycle.

headline: PULLBACK IS TEMPORARY: Three-Pillar Gold Demand Structure — Central Banks, China/India Retail, Fear Trade — All Intact
snippet: Richard Mills argues on June 11 that gold and silver's June correction is a temporary interruption rather than a structural reversal, because all three demand drivers that pushed gold above $5,000 remain fully intact: central bank gold purchases at historically elevated levels (850 tonnes in 2025), simultaneous Chinese and Indian retail demand operating in the same cycle for the first time, and fear-trade positioning tied to US fiscal expansion and dollar debasement concerns that no rate announcement has resolved. Mills specifically calls out Fed Chair Warsh as unlikely to tighten aggressively into a supply-shock-driven inflation, because doing so would amplify the stagflation risk that physical gold was built to hedge — and concludes that institutional strategists expecting gold higher throughout 2026 are reflecting a fundamentally different macro view than the short-term trader capitulation currently visible in the Bullish Percent Index.

headline: 90m AT 0.74% Cu FROM 726m DEPTH: Ero Copper SE Zone Pushes 115m Down-Dip at Furnas, Carajás
snippet: Ero Copper Corp. (TSX: ERO) released on June 10 an additional 24,000 metres of assay results from the Furnas Copper-Gold Project in Brazil's Carajás Mineral Province — bringing total drilling to over 75,000 metres across 10 rigs. Standout hole FURN-DD-00357 cut 90 metres grading 0.74% Cu, 0.5 g/t Au, and 3.18 g/t Ag from 726 metres depth, including 32 metres at 1.17% Cu, 0.68 g/t Au, and 5.40 g/t Ag, extending the SE Zone approximately 115 metres down-dip beyond the current inferred resource boundary; a second step-out pushed approximately 80 metres beyond the resource outline, confirming the deposit remains open at depth and along strike. Ero is completing its full three-programme earn-in from Vale approximately two years ahead of schedule — an execution pace that, against Jefferies' forecast of a 491,000-tonne annual copper deficit through 2030, positions Furnas as a potential resource cornerstone well ahead of the originally anticipated timeline.

headline: PITCHBLENDE AT UNCONFORMITY + 300m STEP-OUT: F4 Uranium Extends Murphy Lake Corridor in Athabasca Basin
snippet: F4 Uranium Corp. (TSXV: FFU) released on June 9 results from step-out holes ML26-017 and ML26-018 at the Murphy Lake uranium project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — drilled approximately 300 metres along strike from previous intercepts and both intersecting anomalous radioactivity (up to 460 cps and 350 cps) over graphitic and sulphide-rich deformation zones in basement rocks, extending the mineralized corridor by 300 metres. This follows the June 2 announcement of hole ML26-015, which intercepted visually identified pitchblende within 3 metres of the basement unconformity at 320.2 metres depth — a mineral association diagnostic of the Athabasca Basin's high-grade unconformity-style uranium deposits. The approximately $2 million program is fully funded by UraniumX Discovery Corp. under an earn-in agreement, with F4 acting as operator. A 300-metre strike extension from pitchblende-bearing holes is the vectoring pattern that historically precedes high-grade unconformity discovery in the Athabasca Basin.

headline: 1.4km STRIKE CONFIRMED IN BOTSWANA: Eastport Completes Foley Uranium Fence 1 — 7 of 16 Holes Hit >200ppm U₃O₈
snippet: Eastport Critical Metals Corp. (TSXV: EVI) announced on June 9 the second batch of assay results from the Foley Uranium Project in Botswana's Kalahari Basin — completing Fence 1 and confirming significant uranium mineralisation across a full 1.4 kilometres of strike length with 7 of 16 drill holes intercepting the >200ppm U₃O₈ threshold. Best intervals include RC034 returning 6.0 metres at 203 ppm U₃O₈ (including 3.0 metres at 273 ppm) and RC037 delivering 2.0 metres at 241.5 ppm and a separate 2.0 metres at 450 ppm U₃O₈; the system remains open to the north, south, and east. The Kalahari Basin has historically produced large-tonnage, bulk-mineable uranium deposits, and a 1.4-kilometre fence with >200ppm continuity in 44% of holes defines the kind of broad mineralised footprint that characterises a scalable resource rather than a narrow vein-hosted target.

headline: MEXICO GOLD MERGE: Gold Resource Corp Shareholders Vote July 2 on Goldgroup Acquisition — Don David + San Francisco Combined
snippet: Gold Resource Corporation (NYSE American: GORO) has scheduled a Special Meeting of Shareholders for July 2, 2026 to vote on the proposed acquisition by Goldgroup Mining Inc. — at a ratio of 1.4476 Goldgroup shares per Gold Resource share, subject to a pre-closing Goldgroup share consolidation. The deal combines Gold Resource's Don David Gold Mine in Oaxaca, Mexico with Goldgroup's San Francisco mine and Cerro Prieto mine, creating a consolidated multi-mine Mexican gold producer with diversified production from two operating assets. With gold at approximately $4,200/oz and Mexican gold producers benefiting from favourable local operating costs and the peso's relative weakness, the merged entity would be better positioned to sustain production, attract institutional capital, and support shareholder returns through a structurally favourable gold price environment heading into H2 2026.

headline: PHASE II DRILLS TURN IN SONORA: Algo Grande Doubles Historical Drilling at Cerro Grande Cu-Ag-Au Skarn, Adelita
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Algo Grande Copper
snippet: Algo Grande Copper Corp. (TSXV: ALGR) announced on June 12 that drilling has commenced on its 8,000-metre Phase II program at the Adelita Project in Sonora, Mexico — the company's largest initiative to date, effectively doubling all historical drilling on the property. Major Drilling Group International spudded hole AG_GC_PH2_001 on June 9 at the Cerro Grande copper-silver-gold skarn target, designed to extend the discovery 100 metres north of the Phase I drill footprint along the 2.5-kilometre corridor defined by magnetics, soil geochemistry, and mapping. Phase II also includes maiden drill tests at the Cerro Potrero South skarn and Las Trancas epithermal targets — making this a true multi-target program that could simultaneously expand the Cerro Grande discovery and open new mineralised systems across Adelita's prospective land package in a proven Sonoran copper district.

headline: LITHIUM TRIANGLE, TWO RIGS ACTIVE: NOA Lithium Drilling Both Wells Simultaneously at Rio Grande Salar, Argentina
source_name: Junior Mining Network / NOA Lithium Brines
snippet: NOA Lithium Brines Inc. (TSXV: NOAL) confirmed on June 11 that both wells in its 2026 exploration drilling program at the Rio Grande Project in Salta Province, Argentina are advancing simultaneously — RT-RG26-PW001 at 168 metres depth and RT-RG26-PW002 at 30 metres depth — accelerating the timeline to define brine aquifer geometry ahead of resource estimation. NOA holds one of the largest lithium brine portfolios in the Lithium Triangle, with over 140,000 hectares across the Rio Grande, Arizaro, and Salinas Grandes salars. With lithium carbonate above $24,000/tonne representing the commercial viability threshold for Argentine brine operations, and the Lithium Triangle attracting accelerated supply-chain investment from battery manufacturers and automakers, a simultaneous two-rig program positions NOA for a potential maiden resource update in the coming quarters.
